Whenever a player has a joke they will step forward and portray the world’s worst version of the suggestion. The referee can get suggestions of occupations, a product or location to give ad slogans for, or an event where things are said. The referee may change the suggestion whenever they wish.
variations:
- May be played with the referee getting only locations and events, with the players telling us things you would never hear there. (Called “Things You Never Hear”)
- May be played with the referee getting only suggestions of products and locations. (Called “Slogans”)
- May be played with the referee getting only suggestions of locations. (Called “Punnsylvania”)

title: FORREST GUMP
description: The referee gets a suggestion. In the style of Forrest Gump’s “Life is like a box of chocolates,” a player creates a setup using “Life is like a box of [suggestion].” The audience asks, “How’s that?” and the player delivers the punchline. Example: If the suggestion is apple: “Life is like a box of apples.” “How’s that?” “It was recommended by my granny Smith!”

title: THE HARRY
description: It’s Switch Left, but also a Micro Harold. The first pairing must perform two dimes for their scene, the second pairing must perform analogous scenes, and the third pairing must perform tangential scenes. If there is a fourth pairing, it must be a genre replay. At any point, the referee can call any of the traditional switches or GROUP, which means all players must do a quick group game before returning to their formation.

title: MUSICAL QUESTIONS?
description: Questions Only, but musical.

title: STRING OF PEARLS FUGUE
description: String of Pearls, but every person sings a rhymed couplet. At the end, everyone sings together as a fugue.
specialNote: May be played as either a Team Game or a Head-to-Head Game.

title: I’M NO EXPERT
description: A pun game set up with the phrase, “Well, I’m no expert…” followed by a pun. Example: “Well, I’m no banana expert… I never found it very appealing.”

title: HERE ME OUT!
description: The referee asks for a well-known movie. Players create a pitch for the next remake of that movie using a pun.

title: THREE HEADED BLUES SINGER
description: Three players take turns singing lines of a three-verse, 12-bar blues song. Every verse, the players rotate.

title: PRODUCER’S PITCH
description: A musical, impression, and guessing game. Two writers pitch a new musical to a producer who has their own ideas. The producer must guess the celebrity who will be stunt-cast as the lead, the lead character’s want or dream for the musical, and the genre of music. The producer has two minutes to guess. Once completed, one or both writers sing the hit song based on the answers, right or wrong.
specialNote: Submitted under “Something else.” Categorized as Guessing Games for review.

title: SONGBOOK
description: One player justifies for three players with limited ability to dialogue. Assign a popular music artist or band to each dialogue-limited player. Those players use the Genius app, or a similar lyrics source, to access the artist’s songs and may speak only by reading or reciting lyrics. The players can be assigned artists they are comfortable with or artists whose lyrics they have not read before.
specialNote: Inspired by games such as Comic Book, Text Line, or Pick-A-Play. A phone or similar device with access to song lyrics is required for each dialogue-limited player.

title: GOONIES
description: Use the structure of Interrogation, but make it Goonies. Players take on big characters in the spirit of the movie, such as Mouth, Data, or Chunk. The guesser tries to decipher the map while the other players drop clues. The guesser must determine: What is the buried treasure? Where in town is it buried? Who is the celebrity trying to stop you?

title: TELENOVELA
description: Requires an offstage guitar player, either a referee or music director. A spinoff of New Choice. Get the title of a soap opera, then two or three players begin a fairly low-stakes scene. The referee or music director may interrupt at any time with a Spanish guitar sting, at which point the stakes increase. The game continues through multiple scene transitions until the stakes can go no higher. It usually ends with a ridiculous scenario involving every player onstage, such as a large family confrontation, a ruined wedding, or similar.
specialNote: Do not appropriate Spanish accents for this game.

title: DOOM SCROLL
description: The referee gets an audience volunteer and asks about them for approximately 30 seconds. The volunteer, or “loyal fan,” sits center stage. Each team creates short reels, ads, dance videos, or other approximately 20–30-second scenes for the loyal fan. The referee blows the whistle and prompts the fan to react. A thumbs-up earns one point, a thumbs-down loses one point, and a heart earns three points. The game may lead into another segment or end a match.
specialNote: There are opportunities for gifts and callbacks, such as one team stitching the other team’s video, parodying a previous video, or creating related commercials and apology videos.

title: BAFTA-WINNING MOMENT
description: Oscar-Winning Moment, but the moments are Shakespearean monologues.

title: CELL [BLACK] TANGO
description: A musical parody of the song “Cell Block Tango” from Chicago!

title: THANKSGIVING LEFTOVERS
description: The audience says, “Happy Thanksgiving!” A player replies, “I brought the [suggestion] casserole,” followed by a punchline.

title: TRICK-OR-TREAT
description: The audience says, “Trick-or-Treat!” A player asks, “Oh my goodness, look at you in your [suggestion] costume—[punchline].” The suggestion is a type of job.

title: SEVERANCE
description: The referee gets a suggestion of a type of job. One team performs a scene as the “outies,” with everyone dealing with a form of consequence such as affliction, injury, or internal turmoil, but with no memory of how they got it. The other team then performs a scene as the “innies,” showing how those afflictions, injuries, or other consequences happened. The same person must play the corresponding “innie” and “outie” on both teams.

title: 99 PROBLEMS
description: A rap-and-rhyme game inspired by Beastie Rap. One person sets up the rhyme for the team and the others pass it down the line until someone drops it. The next team then goes. The team with the most successful rhymes earns the points.

title: SHARK TANK
description: The game gets a product, usually an object; an alteration, such as a drill powered by envy; and an alternate form of currency, such as looking for a 10% investment of Unicorn Tears. The guesser is the presenter, while the Sharks provide the clues.

title: LEXICON
description: One player begins and ends with the same line of dialogue. A second player begins and ends each line with the same word. A third player begins and ends each line with the same letter. If a fourth player is used, the audience provides a “wild card” word or short phrase that player must include each time they speak.

title: DISS TRACK
description: Designed as an opening Head-to-Head Game, the teams rap back and forth in couplets, dissing their opponents. The referee gets a topic for each team, usually stereotypical rivalries such as Cowboys versus Indians. When a player cannot produce a couplet, fails to rhyme, or goes off-topic, that player is eliminated. The final team with players remaining wins.

title: BOB ROSS
description: The referee gets new suggestions after each elimination. A player says, “Bob Ross—look at the happy little [suggestion],” then delivers a punchline. Example: “Look at the happy banana. I’m not going to paint just one. Let’s paint bunches.”

title: PUT ME IN COACH
description: A player says, “Put me in, coach! I’m the best [suggestion] on the team,” followed by a punchline. Example: “I’ll make the opposing team split!”

title: SING OF THE HILL
description: Played like Challenge. One person sings a song to impress a judge. A player from the back line may interrupt and upstage the current singer, taking over the song. The last player singing wins if the judge likes them, although the game may end with everyone singing together in a tableau. The game is scored by who sang last or who performed better.

title: SARDINES
description: Replay the scene while reducing the playing area by 50% each time.

title: ROXANNE
refereeIntroduction: Players will perform a scene while the song, "Roxanne" performs in the background of the scene. Everytime Sting sings "Roxanne" the players must do a physical action and justify why they are doing that action. The song is not meant to be a part of the scene.
variations: Can we played where each player gets a different action to act out.

title: THIS JUST IN
refereeIntroduction: “The players will deliver breaking news inspired by your suggestions.”
description: Both teams line up along the back wall. The referee gets a suggestion, and players step forward one at a time to deliver a breaking-news report beginning with “This just in...” and ending with a punchline based on the suggestion. The referee may collect a new suggestion whenever needed.

title: POD PEOPLE
refereeIntroduction: “Two players will only be able to speak using words from a podcast, while another player makes it all make sense.”
description: Two players wear headphones and listen to a podcast selected by the audience. Those players may use only words and phrases they hear in the podcast as dialogue. A third player may speak freely and must justify the borrowed dialogue so the scene remains coherent.
specialNote: Requires two wireless or Bluetooth headsets and access to podcast audio.

title: INTERROWOP
refereeIntroduction: “The players will solve a musical mystery through an a cappella interrogation.”
description: One player exits while the referee gets three pieces of information: what the player stole, who they stole it from, and where they hid it. When the player returns, the teammates provide rhyming clues through an a cappella interrogation sung to the tune of “Runaround Sue.” Each clue-giver uses an AABB rhyme scheme. Once the player believes they know the answers, they sing a confession using their own AABB rhyme scheme.
specialNote: The source specifies a four-player team. The referee may award points for correct guesses in addition to audience voting.

title: LYRICS ONLY
refereeIntroduction: “Some players will only be able to speak in song lyrics.”
description: One player may speak freely and serves as the justifier. The remaining players may speak only in recognizable song lyrics. The justifier incorporates those lyrics into the scene and helps the dialogue make sense.
variations: May be played as a Head-To-Head Game with one player from each team. Both players may speak only in song lyrics. A player rotates out after hesitating or using dialogue that is not a lyric; the other player repeats the last lyric as the first line of a new scene. The team with the fewest rotations wins.

title: SEUSS SWITCH
refereeIntroduction: “The scene will switch between ordinary dialogue and the rhyming world of Dr. Seuss.”
description: The players begin a scene using ordinary dialogue and behavior. Whenever the referee whistles or calls “Seuss,” the players immediately switch into an exaggerated Dr. Seuss-inspired style using rhyming couplets, slant rhymes, invented words, animated voices, and cartoonish physicality. When the referee switches them back, the players return to the ordinary version of the scene.

title: MAGIC 8 BALL
refereeIntroduction: “The players will show us two different answers to the same question.”
description: Two players begin a scene while two additional players wait on the sidelines. When one character asks a yes-or-no question, the asking player remains in the scene and the other player exits. A sideline player enters and the scene continues to an ending based on one answer. The scene then restarts from the question, the sideline players switch, and the alternate answer leads to a different ending.

title: INCEPTION MANUAL
refereeIntroduction: “The players will tell a story that keeps falling into deeper and deeper dreams.”
description: The teams create a conducted story about a dream. Details introduced in one section inspire the next dream or chapter when the conductor calls on another player. Each new section becomes another layer of the dream, building a nested story until the conductor brings the narrative to a conclusion.

title: FLYERER
refereeIntroduction: “The players will pitch shows inspired by your suggestions.”
description: Both teams line up along the back wall. The referee gets a suggestion, and a player steps forward to ask, “Do you want to see a show about [suggestion]?” The audience responds, “What’s it about?” and the player delivers the punchline. The referee may collect a new suggestion whenever needed.

title: WOOZY BABY
refereeIntroduction: “The players will turn an ordinary scene into a 1920s jazz performance whenever called upon.”
description: The players begin a scene normally. Whenever the referee calls for it, the scene shifts into the style of a 1920s jazz chanteuse, with the players singing and performing in an exaggerated vintage style. The referee may switch between the normal scene and the musical style throughout the game.

title: RATINGS REPLAY
refereeIntroduction: “The players will replay the same scene with increasingly extreme ratings.”
description: The team performs a short, completely innocent G-rated scene. The scene is then replayed as PG-13, R, and finally an invented “XXX” interpretation. Each replay keeps the basic scene recognizable while escalating the style and content according to the announced rating.
variations: May be played as a Head-To-Head Game.
specialNote: Designed for a Blue show rather than a competitive match. The final “XXX” replay must remain non-pornographic; the host should invent a playful alternate meaning, such as characters from the movie xXx or lumberjacks using axes.

title: RECIPE BLOG
refereeIntroduction: “The players will tell a story in the style of an overly detailed online recipe blog.”
description: The teams create a conducted story using the structure and style of an online recipe blog. The story may include a long personal introduction, elaborate descriptions of ingredients, excessively detailed preparation instructions, and reader comments. The referee conducts the players through the different sections of the blog.

title: CONNECT FOUR
refereeIntroduction: “The team will perform four different one-minute games in four minutes.”
description: The team performs four one-minute games in immediate succession. The specific games may vary, but one suggested sequence is a one-minute scene, a one-minute replay, a one-minute song, and a one-minute pun game. Each segment ends at one minute and transitions directly into the next.
specialNote: Designed primarily for classes or late shows rather than a traditional match.

title: ROM COM
refereeIntroduction: “The players will create an entire romantic comedy in five scenes.”
description: The referee gets a job, a hobby, and three date locations. Two players become the romantic leads, with one endowed by the job and the other by the hobby. A third player portrays best friends and supporting characters. The game follows five scenes: brief introductions of each lead, a meet-cute, a silent date montage across the three locations, a complication that separates the couple, and a final reconciliation in which the leads confess their love.
variations: The date montage may be accompanied by an upbeat romantic-comedy song. The final blackout line may be a pun based on the job, hobby, or date locations.
specialNote: The source recommends keeping the two opening scenes under 30 seconds, the meet-cute and montage near one minute each, and the complete game around four to five minutes.

title: PYGMALION
refereeIntroduction: “The players’ status will change whenever they are given a new accent.”
description: Two players begin a scene with a clear difference in status. At any time, the referee may call “Pygmalion” and name a player. That player immediately adopts a new accent, and the change in accent signals a change in the character’s status. The referee continues calling new accents as the scene develops and additional characters enter.
specialNote: Players should avoid using accents as stereotypes or caricatures of cultures or ethnicities.

title: WHICH IS ALSO A...
refereeIntroduction: “The players will name items that belong to a category. At any time, I may ask, ‘Which is also a...?’ The player must use their previous answer to create a new category, and the game will continue from there.”
description: The players line up at the front of the stage. The referee gets a broad category from the audience and points to players one at a time. Each player must quickly name an item that belongs in the current category. At any time, after a player gives an answer that could also belong to another category, the referee may ask, “Which is also a...?” The player must identify another meaningful category that includes their answer. That answer becomes the first example in the new category, and play immediately continues using the new category. For example, if the category is Cats and a player says “Jaguar,” the referee may ask, “Which is also a...?” The player might answer “Sports team,” changing the category to Sports Teams. A player is eliminated for hesitating, repeating an answer, giving an answer that does not fit the current category, or failing to provide a valid new category when prompted. Play continues until one player remains.
variations: - Players may receive one warning before elimination. - The game may be played without elimination as a speed and association exercise. - The referee may allow the audience to shout “Which is also a...?” when they recognize a possible connection.
specialNote: New categories should be broad, recognizable groupings with multiple possible answers. Arbitrary descriptions such as “words with seven letters” should generally not be accepted. The referee should call for a category change when an answer offers a clear and entertaining connection or when the current category begins to lose momentum.
